title: Assess Wilber’s methodology and epistemic claims
description:
Examine methodological and epistemic critiques of Wilber’s project: use of sources, synthesis across disciplines, treatment of scientific evidence, falsifiability, and the difference between speculative philosophy, interpretive framework, and empirical theory.

Include serious criticisms such as Jeff Meyerhoff’s scholarship critique where warranted, and present Wilber’s own framing or defenses where primary sources support them. Produce a fair account of the tradeoffs of ambitious synthesis rather than assuming either that synthesis is invalid or that breadth substitutes for evidence.

title: Assess evidence behind Wilber and Integral empirical claims
description:
Assess the evidential basis for major empirical claims made by Wilber and Integral Theory. Prioritize claims about developmental stages, cultural evolution, historical population distributions (for example claims about the prevalence of particular value stages in an era), and the empirical standing of models such as Spiral Dynamics.

For each case, locate the original claim and cited support, evaluate the quality and scope of the evidence, identify serious published criticism and relevant defenses, and explain what conclusion the evidence can actually bear. Avoid reproducing striking numerical claims without a verifiable source trail.

title: Build a fair critical layer for Wilber and Integral Theory
description:
Build a substantial, fair critical layer for Wilber and Integral Theory. The aim is neither apologetics nor a catalogue of objections: distinguish what a criticism actually establishes, the strength of its evidence, Wilber’s relevant replies, and the limits of both.

Start with evidence and methodology, then develop thematic and stylistic/reception strands. Link critiques to the relevant concepts and works rather than treating criticism as a detached afterthought. Maintain a clear distinction between sourced factual claims, interpretation, and open questions.

## Request context

Begin with evidential criticism: strong empirical claims in Wilber, including claims about cultural evolution or historical population distributions (for example, the share of a population at an Orange stage around the American Revolution), and the evidence for Spiral Dynamics. Build an extensive but fair critique that also examines method, thematic claims, style, and possible defenses. The treatment should recognize that Wilber may at times be a speculative philosopher and synthesiser, while still asking what his evidence supports. Include a curated external-readings route and writers who offer useful work on Wilber or Integral.

title: Integrate hosted notes into the wiki knowledge graph
description:
Integrate the existing hosted notes and write-ups by Rufus, Catherine Tran, and Rosie Bell into the wiki’s navigation and knowledge graph. They currently live in `notes/` as clearly attributed verbatim material and are mainly reached from their associated work pages.

Map each note’s substantive concepts, people, works, and claims; add selective reciprocal wikilinks where the relationship is real; and make useful discovery paths from the relevant concept/people/work pages. Preserve attribution, original context, and the boundary between an author’s note and the wiki’s own synthesis. Do not turn incidental topical overlap into indiscriminate links.

## Request context

Migrate the notes and write-ups presently linked as external material by Rufus and others into the site more fully: not just references, but useful wiki-style cross-links that make the material discoverable and connected.

title: Audit co-authored and pseudonymous Wilber works

Decide how each relationship should be represented in `works/` frontmatter and reader-facing copy (contributors, authorship/byline note, format, date, editions). Check the full catalog for comparable cases so the treatment is consistent. Do not infer that a contributor credit or pen name represents a solo Wilber work without evidence.

See docs/plans/2026-09-14-works-bibliography-audit.md. Pseudonymous additions remain for this bead.

title: Link excerpt attributions to their public work pages

Make the cited work title in each attribution a link to its public `works/<slug>.md` page. This gives readers a stable bibliographic destination without exposing raw full-text files, which production deliberately excludes. Preserve chapter/footnote detail and quote verification; add a shared authoring convention or automated check so future excerpts do not regress.

Future annotation pages may offer chapter-level reading links where a public annotated text exists, but this task should not publish `library/` or link to raw source files.

title: Map the Integral ecosystem and documented impact
description:
Map the broader impact of Integral Theory across organisations, professional fields, communities, and public discourse. Research institutions, projects, teaching/practice communities, and cultural outputs with evidence of direct Integral lineage or uptake.

title: Research the impact and influence of Wilber and Integral Theory
description:
Research and document the impact and influence of Wilber and Integral Theory. Build a sourced, discriminating account of who and what was influenced, how direct the connection is, what changed in practice or thought, and where claims of influence are weak or merely adjacent.

Cover public intellectuals and creators, institutions and fields, media/cultural work, and the wider Integral ecosystem. Treat influence as a claim requiring evidence, not a branding exercise; distinguish personal acknowledgement, conceptual similarity, collaboration, and demonstrable downstream impact.

## Request context

Document notable people who mention or are influenced by Wilber, beginning with possible cases such as Mark Manson, and cultural impact including claims about the Matrix creators. Also investigate other writing about Integral and its wider impact, evidence, and influence. The aim is to make the extent and nature of influence visible without overstating it.

title: Document influential figures and cultural works

title: Curate external readings on Wilber and Integral Theory
description:
Curate a selective external readings list for Wilber and Integral Theory: rigorous criticism, useful introductions, sympathetic but non-promotional interpretations, and strong contemporary writing by people who engage seriously with the tradition.

Each entry should explain why it is worth reading, its stance or relationship to Wilber, author/date/source, and the relevant wiki pages. Keep the list intentionally small and maintained rather than a link dump; include writers who discuss Integral well even when they are not direct Wilber scholars.

title: Develop thematic and stylistic critiques of Wilber
description:
Develop thematic and stylistic/reception critiques of Wilber and Integral Theory. Cover significant topic-specific disputes (for example cultural evolution, hierarchy, gender, ecology, spirituality, and politics) as evidence supports them, alongside critiques of prose style, rhetoric, audience, and guru culture.

Organize by concrete claims and works, distinguish internal Integral disagreements from external criticism, and link to relevant concept/people/work pages. Pair each criticism with the strongest reasonable response or limitation where available.

title: Resolve remaining publication records and compare retitled editions
description: Follow residual research in docs/plans/2026-09-14-works-bibliography-audit.md. Locate actual publisher/file for The Integral Approach (2013); resolve 2005/2006 Starter Kit release and complete kit/IOS credits; inspect original audio packaging and draft descriptions. Compare 2017/2024 Post-Truth editions and 2014/2018 Fourth Turning/Integral Buddhism texts before labeling revisions minor or substantial. Record exact evidence and update public notes. Basic guide delivery does not depend on resolving every gap: uncertainty is currently explicit.

title: Add a consolidated cross-book People Index overview
description:
Design and add a consolidated overview at the top of the People Index while retaining the separate, per-book rosters. The overview should make it easy to see each person’s combined presence across source books—for example, unique-page totals and a sortable or readable table with per-book counts and an overall total—without obscuring the book-specific context and peak chapters below.

Define how duplicate names, name-drops, new source books, and incomplete scans are handled. Prefer a maintainable source-of-truth or generation approach over manually keeping several count tables in sync.

title: Add public-domain portraits to substantive people pages
description:
Source suitable public-domain images from Wikimedia Commons/Wikipedia for the people pages Wilber substantively discusses. Create a consistent asset and attribution/provenance pattern, record each source and licence, and add images where they improve the page without making the index visually heavy.

Start with a small representative set to validate rendering, licensing metadata, and crop treatment before expanding across the full roster. Do not use images with unclear reuse rights or introduce portraits for the deliberately unprofiled name-drops.

title: Explore an optional network map of wiki connections
description:
Investigate a small, optional visual map of the wiki's connections. The existing roadmap is a curated linear route with named branches; a graph should complement that experience, not replace or visually overwhelm it.

Start with a design/spike: derive a typed graph from the existing `See Also` wikilinks and `works:` metadata; test an accessible, responsive rendering compatible with Flowershow; and evaluate a limited route such as `/explore` or a small homepage/roadmap invitation. Avoid a full-bleed graph on the homepage until the interaction and mobile behavior have been reviewed. Nodes should link through to their pages, and the graph must retain a usable non-JavaScript/textual alternative.

title: Make the Works catalog introduction reader-facing
description:
The opening of the public Works catalog currently explains internal page structure and editorial workflow: file paths, frontmatter fields, where cover provenance is kept, and what `status: draft` means. It is useful project documentation but does not help a reader choose a book.

Replace it with a short reader-facing introduction and retain the useful `core` marker explanation. Move maintainership details about the schema, cover-source ledger, and verification state into an appropriate internal document. Keep the chronological catalog intact.

Related to the works validation and reading-guides epic.
close_reason: Replaced catalog introduction with reader-facing guide links and scope/core explanations; maintainership schema, verification and provenance conventions now in docs/works-catalog.md. Chronology preserved; verification passed.

title: Explore a visual timeline of Wilber works, phases and themes
description:
Deferred idea requested during bibliography planning, not immediate implementation. See docs/plans/2026-09-14-works-reading-guides-research.md. Explore an elegant timeline with phase bands, theme filters, contribution types and edition/abridgment relationships. Base it on validated metadata, retain text access and the chronological index, and show uncertain boundaries honestly.

Implementation plan: docs/plans/2026-09-14-works-reading-guides-implementation.md. Follow the matching task and acceptance criteria.

Expanded brief: create a striking map of how books descend from and build on earlier works, combined with publication time and Wilber phase bands. Explore a branching graph rather than a strict tree because works may have multiple predecessors. Distinguish retitling, minor/substantial revision, abridgment, anthology extraction, and conceptual development/application. Source each connection; distinguish documented reuse from editorial inference and show unknown revision extent honestly. Consider theme filtering, book details, mobile/keyboard access, a text alternative and a shareable static export. Begin after the basic phase and annotated bibliography pages. Explore visual concepts before choosing implementation; do not promise traffic outcomes.
notes: Research and design handoff: docs/plans/2026-09-17-wilber-works-visualization-research-and-design.md. Execute child Beads in dependency order. The first ready task is wilberwiki-at6.4.1. Production implementation is explicitly out of scope until Rufus approves the information architecture at wilberwiki-at6.4.6.

comments.author: Rufus Pollock
comments.text: Design reset after initial visual concepts were rejected. The visualization must be driven by job stories and a sourced data model before visual styling. Current repo has strong bibliographic coverage for 40 title/edition pages and a sourced five-phase overview, but its 45 concept pages cite only SES (1995) and Integral Psychology (2000); it cannot yet support claims about when concepts first emerged across 1977–2024. Research precedents point toward a top-down, SVG-based idea map with a composed static overview plus interaction/share export. Especially relevant: Stemma (source and confidence on every edge), Histomaps (time as top-down streams, overview plus semantic zoom and explicit share graphic), Shape of Song (recurrence across a sequence), and philosophy maps (semantic versus influence views, plus a warning about unreadable hairballs). Next step is to define job stories, concept/work relationship schema, key-work research sample, and acceptance criteria before choosing a visual form.
